summary: Configured node1, node2, and node3 as a persistent MariaDB 10.11/Galera 4 cluster. All members are currently active, Primary, Synced, ready, and report cluster size 3 with identical data. Single-member availability, automatic resynchronization, and rolling reboot persistence were verified.
actions_performed: Installed MariaDB, Galera, and rsync on all nodes.
Configured node-specific Galera membership, rsync state transfer, recoverable gcache, causal reads, automatic service restart, and boot-time enablement.
Verified writes through every member replicate to every other member.
Stopped node3, confirmed node1/node2 remained writable with quorum, then verified node3 automatically caught up on return.
Generated node-local verification credentials without exposing them.
Restarted node1, node2, and node3 sequentially, restoring full cluster health before each subsequent restart.

evidence.requirement: Persistent three-member MariaDB Galera configuration and final health
evidence.summary: Final runtime state on every private TCP endpoint is active, wsrep-enabled, Primary, Synced, ready, and cluster size 3 with identical five-row data.

evidence.requirement: Writes through any member are available from the others
evidence.summary: node1, node2, and node3 each committed a unique row; all three members subsequently returned the identical three-row set.

evidence.requirement: Database remains available with one member unavailable
evidence.summary: node3 was inactive with no SQL listener while node1 and node2 remained Primary, Synced, ready at size 2 and accepted mutually visible writes.
After returning, node3 automatically became active, Synced, Primary, ready at size 3 and contained both rows committed during its absence.
Healthy baseline and restart acknowledgement captured; boot ID changed from 17b362d1… to 98972374…, followed by active/enabled MariaDB, complete data, and size-3 recovery.
